title: How to Reduce Tightness After Tummy Tuck?
meta_description: Tightness comes from muscle repair, the closed skin and swelling, and eases over weeks or months. What helps, what to wear and when to call.
excerpt: Why a tummy tuck feels tight, how long the pulling lasts, why the stomach can feel hard, what to wear and when stretching is safe, with the signs that mean a call to your surgeon.
quick_answer:
How do you reduce tightness after a tummy tuck?

Tightness comes from muscle repair, the closed skin and swelling, and eases as they heal. Walk bent at the waist for 7 to 10 days, wear your garment as directed, usually 4 to 6 weeks, and stretch only once your surgeon clears it. Swelling keeps easing until about 3 months (Cindy Wu, MD, on the ASPS website).

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Cindy Wu, MD
sources.title: Answers to common tummy tuck questions (2019)
quotes: After surgery, you will be placed in a compression garment, which will be worn for 4-6 weeks after surgery to help with reducing swelling.
You will be bent at the waist while standing or lying down for 7-10 days after surgery to protect the incision and to allow for your skin to adapt.
After this time, you will be able to stand up straight.
The bruising will subside in a couple of weeks, and the swelling will continue to diminish until approximately three months post-procedure.
You can walk the day of surgery.
In fact, most plastic surgeons encourage patients to walk three times the day of surgery to improve blood circulation to keep the risk of blood clots in the legs to a minimum.
Adequate hydration and ambulation are also important to lower the risk of blood clots after surgery.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck
quotes: Tummy tuck surgery, also known as abdominoplasty, removes excess fat and skin and, in most cases, restores weakened or separated muscles creating an abdominal profile that is smoother and firmer.

sources.title: What results can I expect from a tummy tuck?
quotes: Within a week or two, you should be standing tall and confident in your new slimmer profile.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Shahram Salemy, MD
sources.title: What you need to know about your tummy tuck recovery (2019)
quotes: Some people experience numbness or a pulling sensation for weeks or months after a tummy tuck, but this is typically normal and often fades with time.
After the procedure is complete, your surgeon will discuss a more specific timeline for your recovery, but generally speaking, most patients begin feeling more normal around the eight-week mark.
You will have an abdominal support garment or wrap that will help with swelling and discomfort during recovery, so it's important to wear it for the recommended amount of time each day.

sources.publisher: ASPS website, a post by Samir Rao, MD
sources.title: Understanding the different types of tummy tucks (2024)
quotes: Most patients can return to nonstrenuous work after a couple of weeks, but it takes around three months to fully recover from a tummy tuck.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck (Abdominoplasty)
quotes: You may feel a tightness or pulling sensation around your abdomen as you heal.
This will go away.
Achieving proper nutrition can help your body heal.

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Scar
quotes: Avoid heavy lifting, strenuous exercise, sexual activity and stretching until your provider says it’s safe to do these activities (usually four to eight weeks after the procedure).

sources.title: Tummy Tuck Aftercare & Recovery
quotes: Other red flags include shortness of breath, chest pains, and an unusual heartbeat.
Call your surgeon immediately if you notice an increase in swelling, pain, redness, drainage, or bleeding in the surgical area, or if you develop fever, dizziness, nausea, or vomiting.
You will also need to wear a wide elastic compression garment to reduce swelling and provide support to the skin as it tightens.
It is important to walk to discourage swelling and to prevent blood clots in the legs.
It is also important to know that the amount of time it takes for recovery varies greatly among individuals.
